scenarios.title: Standard 1% Risk on Major Pair
scenarios.questionText: Account Balance: $10,000. Risk Rule: 1% max per trade ($100). EUR/USD Stop Distance: 50 pips. Standard pip value is $10/lot. What is your correct lot size?
scenarios.explanation: Risk Amount = $10,000 × 1% = $100. Position Size = Risk ($100) ÷ (Stop Pips (50) × $10/pip/lot) = 100 ÷ 500 = 0.20 Lots (2 Mini Lots / 20,000 units).
scenarios.learningObjective: Calculate exact lot size using account equity, percentage risk, and stop distance.

scenarios.title: 2% Risk with Tight 20-Pip Scalp Stop

scenarios.learningObjective: Adjust lot size upward when stop distance is tight without increasing dollar risk.

scenarios.title: Micro Account 1% Sizing

scenarios.title: Structural Invalidation vs Arbitrary Pips
scenarios.questionText: You are planning a Long entry on an uptrend pullback at support (1.0850). Structural swing low is at 1.0832. ATR is 10 pips. Where is the most technically sound stop-loss?
options: 1.0845 (5 pips below entry, regardless of structure)
1.0700 (150 pips away to avoid being stopped out)
scenarios.explanation: A technical stop-loss must be placed where your trade thesis is invalidated (below the swing low at 1.0832), plus a buffer (1.0825) for spread and noise.
scenarios.learningObjective: Distinguish between technical invalidation levels and arbitrary dollar/pip stops.

scenarios.title: Short Trade Resistance Invalidation
scenarios.questionText: You are shorting a breakdown retest at resistance (1.2650). The recent lower high swing peak was made at 1.2678. Where should your stop-loss be positioned?
scenarios.explanation: For short setups, the market invalidates the bearish bias if price breaks above the swing high (1.2678). Placing the stop at 1.2685 protects against noise while keeping invalidation valid.
scenarios.learningObjective: Place short stop-losses above valid structural swing highs.

scenarios.title: The Danger of Moving Stops (Revenge / Hope)
scenarios.questionText: Price is 3 pips away from your predefined stop-loss on a Long trade. The setup has visibly broken structure downwards. What is the disciplined action?
scenarios.correctAnswer: Let the stop trigger and accept the predefined loss
options: Let the stop trigger and accept the predefined loss
Move the stop 30 pips lower so price has room to bounce
Remove the stop completely and wait for a recovery
Double the position size to lower the average entry
scenarios.explanation: Moving a stop-loss when price approaches it converts a controlled 1% loss into an uncontrolled, catastrophic drawdown. Once structure breaks, the thesis is dead.
scenarios.learningObjective: Eliminate the fatal trading mistake of moving or removing active stop-losses.

scenarios.title: Asymmetric Recovery Math (-20% Drawdown)
scenarios.questionText: An account drops 20% from $10,000 to $8,000. What percentage gain is required on the remaining $8,000 balance to recover back to $10,000?
scenarios.explanation: Gain Required = ($10,000 - $8,000) ÷ $8,000 = $2,000 ÷ $8,000 = +25.0%. As drawdown increases, the required recovery percentage grows non-linearly.
scenarios.learningObjective: Understand why percentage recovery demands exceed the original percentage loss.

scenarios.title: The 50% Catastrophe Threshold
scenarios.questionText: An account suffers a 50% drawdown, dropping from $20,000 down to $10,000. What percentage gain is now required just to break even?
scenarios.explanation: To turn $10,000 back into $20,000, you must make $10,000 profit on a $10,000 balance: $10,000 ÷ $10,000 = +100.0%. A 50% loss requires a 100% gain to recover.
scenarios.learningObjective: Recognize that deep drawdowns create nearly insurmountable mathematical recovery hurdles.

scenarios.title: Severe 75% Drawdown Recovery
scenarios.questionText: An account drops 75% (from $100,000 down to $25,000). What percentage gain is required to restore the initial balance?
scenarios.explanation: Gain Required = ($100,000 - $25,000) ÷ $25,000 = $75,000 ÷ $25,000 = +300.0%. This illustrates why capital preservation is the absolute foundation of professional trading.
scenarios.learningObjective: Calculate extreme drawdown recovery demands.

scenarios.correctAnswer: Add to the losing position to lower your average price
options: Add to the losing position to lower your average price
Accept the technical invalidation and exit at the stop
Log the trade in your trading journal with screenshots
scenarios.explanation: Adding to losers multiplies exposure when the market has already proven your timing wrong. Professional traders add to winners, never losers.
scenarios.learningObjective: Recognize why adding to losing trades is an account-fatal habit.

options: Execute the trade with standard or slightly reduced size (0.5%) according to your rules
